# Public data sources for prescription claim adjudication — verified 2026-07-13

**Reachability correction (important):** Contrary to the stated sandbox limits, `download.cms.gov` **and** `downloads.cms.gov` both responded HTTP 200 from this sandbox today (Akamai-fronted), and `data.cms.gov` is reachable too. Only `synthea.mitre.org` remains untested/blocked. This matters because the CMS bulk files live on those hosts — see items 3-5. `api.fda.gov` (openFDA) is also reachable (item 6).

Every curl below was run and returned real data with **no auth header, no cookie, no API key**.

---

## 1. RxNorm via RxNav REST API (no UMLS license)

- **Base URL:** `https://rxnav.nlm.nih.gov/REST/` — no login, no key.
- **Format:** JSON (`.json`) or XML (`.xml`) by suffix.
- **Working calls (all verified):**
  - RxCUI by drug name: `curl "https://rxnav.nlm.nih.gov/REST/rxcui.json?name=warfarin"` → `{"idGroup":{"rxnormId":["11289"]}}`
  - Related brand/generic: `curl "https://rxnav.nlm.nih.gov/REST/rxcui/11289/related.json?tty=BN"` → returned Coumadin (202421), Jantoven (405155). Use `tty=IN` for ingredient, `tty=SCD`/`SBD` for clinical/branded drugs.
  - ATC drug class (RxClass): `curl "https://rxnav.nlm.nih.gov/REST/rxclass/class/byRxcui.json?rxcui=11289&relaSource=ATC"` → classId `B01AA` "Vitamin K antagonists".
  - VA drug class: `curl "https://rxnav.nlm.nih.gov/REST/rxclass/class/byDrugName.json?drugName=warfarin&relaSource=VA"` → classId `BL110` "ANTICOAGULANTS".
- **License/redistribution:** RxNav APIs are free/public; RxNorm content is in the public domain. No UMLS license needed to *call the API*.
- **UMLS confirmation:** The RxNorm **full monthly release** (`https://download.nlm.nih.gov/umls/kss/rxnorm/RxNorm_full_current.zip`) **does require UMLS login/API key** — confirmed on the NLM docs page. Bonus: the **RxNorm Current Prescribable Content** files are documented as "no license required" (host `download.nlm.nih.gov`, not tested for sandbox reachability).
- **Adjudication use:** Normalize the submitted NDC/drug to an ingredient RxCUI, resolve therapeutic class (ATC/VA) to drive drug-allergy and duplicate-therapy/step-therapy rules, and map brand↔generic for formulary/generic-substitution logic.

## 2. ICD-10-CM diagnosis codes in bulk (no login)

**(i) NLM Clinical Tables API** — `https://clinicaltables.nlm.nih.gov/api/icd10cm/v3/search`
- No login/key. Format: JSON array `[total, [codes], null, [[code,name],…]]`.
- Verified: `curl "https://clinicaltables.nlm.nih.gov/api/icd10cm/v3/search?sf=code,name&terms=diabetes&count=3"`
- **Paging:** use `offset` + `count`; `count`/`maxList` max = **500**; documented hard cap **offset+count ≤ 7,500**, and reported totals capped at 10,000. It is a *search/autocomplete* API (requires a `terms` filter) — good for on-demand validation, not a clean full dump. Verified paging: `...?terms=diabetes&maxList=5&offset=3&count=5&sf=code,name`.
- License: free "as is," public domain source data.

**(ii) CDC bulk order files (full code set)** — `https://ftp.cdc.gov/pub/Health_Statistics/NCHS/Publications/ICD10CM/<YEAR>/`
- No login. Directory listing verified. Current-year (FY2026) files:
  - Code descriptions: `https://ftp.cdc.gov/pub/Health_Statistics/NCHS/Publications/ICD10CM/2026/icd10cm-Code%20Descriptions-2026.zip`
  - Tabular + index: `.../2026/icd10cm-table%20and%20index-2026.zip`
  - Addenda: `.../2026/icd10cm-addenda-2026.zip`
  - (FY2025 equivalent: `.../2025/ICD10-CM%20Code%20Descriptions%202025.zip`)
- Format: ZIP of fixed-width/plain-text description files. Public domain.
- **Adjudication use:** Clinical Tables for real-time diagnosis-code validation on the claim; CDC zip to load the complete code set into a reference table for medical-necessity / diagnosis-based edits (prior-auth criteria, NCD/LCD linkage).

## 3. CMS Medicare Part D Formulary PUF (formulary status, tier, PA, step therapy, quantity limits)

- **Dataset landing (data.cms.gov):** `https://data.cms.gov/provider-summary-by-type-of-service/medicare-part-d-prescribers/quarterly-prescription-drug-plan-formulary-pharmacy-network-and-pricing-information` (the www.cms.gov "files-download" page returned 403 to the fetch tool but is a redirect/landing shell — the real files are on `data.cms.gov`).
- **No login, no key** — free downloads (files became free Jan 2021). Discovered via the public catalog `https://data.cms.gov/data.json`.
- **Latest Quarterly PUF (SPUF), verified HTTP 200, 2.5 GB ZIP:** `https://data.cms.gov/sites/default/files/2026-04/65e8dafd-c42b-4c2a-93c2-551bbc80bef9/SPUF_2026_20260408.zip` (prior quarters: `SPUF_2026_20260107.zip`, `SPUF_2025_20251009.zip`, etc.).
- There is also a lighter **Monthly** "Prescription Drug Plan Formulary and Pharmacy Network" PUF: e.g. `https://data.cms.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/.../2026_20260610.zip`.
- **Format:** ZIP of pipe/tab-delimited txt tables — Basic Drugs Formulary file keys on **NDC** with **tier level**, and **prior-authorization / step-therapy / quantity-limit** indicators; plus Plan Info, Geographic Locator, and (quarterly only) a Pricing file (avg monthly unit cost).
- **Alternative host note:** files are on **`data.cms.gov/sites/default/files/...`** (reachable), not `download.cms.gov` — so the sandbox restriction is a non-issue here.
- **License:** CMS public-use file, freely redistributable (US Gov work).
- **Adjudication use:** This is the single richest public source for the actual payer rules you named — real per-plan formulary status, tier, PA flag, step-therapy flag, and quantity-limit flag keyed by NDC. Directly seeds formulary/tier/PA/ST/QL edits.

## 4. CMS NCD/LCD coverage determinations (medical-necessity rules)

- **Bulk export page:** `https://www.cms.gov/medicare-coverage-database/downloads/downloads.aspx` (no login).
- **Direct bulk files, verified HTTP 200 on `downloads.cms.gov`:**
  - NCDs: `https://downloads.cms.gov/medicare-coverage-database/downloads/exports/ncd.zip` (verified: `application/zip`, 1,276,818 bytes, last-modified 2026-07-09).
  - LCDs: `.../exports/current_lcd.zip`, `.../exports/all_lcd.zip`
  - Articles (this is where CPT/HCPCS + ICD-10 code linkages now live): `.../exports/current_article.zip`, `.../exports/all_article.zip`
  - Everything: `.../exports/all_data.zip`
- **Format:** ZIP of relational tables (national download refreshed weekly; local every Thursday). Public domain.
- **Adjudication use:** Load NCD/Article code linkages to drive medical-necessity edits and diagnosis-to-procedure coverage checks; more relevant to medical/Part B claims than pure pharmacy, but useful for PA criteria and B-vs-D coverage determinations.

## 5. NPPES / NPI provider registry

**(a) Real-time API** — `https://npiregistry.cms.hhs.gov/api/` — no login, no key.
- Required param `version=2.1`. Verified queries:
  - By NPI: `curl "https://npiregistry.cms.hhs.gov/api/?version=2.1&number=<10-digit-NPI>"`
  - By attributes: `curl "https://npiregistry.cms.hhs.gov/api/?version=2.1&taxonomy_description=pharmacy&state=CA&limit=1"` → returned full provider record.
- Other params: `enumeration_type` (NPI-1/NPI-2), `first_name`, `last_name`, `organization_name`, `city`, `postal_code`, `taxonomy_description`, `limit` (max 200), `skip` (max 1000). Format: JSON. Rejects malformed NPIs (verified error response).
- **Full data dissemination file (bulk), verified reachable — no login:** monthly full replacement `https://download.cms.gov/nppes/NPPES_Data_Dissemination_July_2026_V2.zip` (HTTP 206 on range request confirmed); weekly incrementals `NPPES_Data_Dissemination_070626_071226_Weekly_V2.zip`; deactivations `NPPES_Deactivated_NPI_Report_071326_V2.zip`. Listing page: `https://download.cms.gov/nppes/NPI_Files.html`. Note V1 files were retired March 2026 — use **V2**.
- **Format:** ZIP → large CSV + readme/code-value/header docs. Public/FOIA-disclosable, freely redistributable.
- **Adjudication use:** Prescriber and pharmacy eligibility/identity validation, taxonomy checks, and active/deactivated status screening on the claim.

## 6. Other useful public pharmacy-adjudication datasets

- **openFDA NDC directory** — `https://api.fda.gov/drug/ndc.json` — **reachable, no key** (key only raises rate limits). All facts below were verified live against the GitHub API/raw source and web search on 2026-07-13.

## 1. SYNTHEA deep-dive (github.com/synthetichealth/synthea)

### Version + JAR asset (confirmed against GitHub Releases API)
- **Latest tagged release: `v4.0.0`** (published 2026-03-05). Also a rolling `master-branch-latest` (built 2026-06-30) that tracks the master branch.
- **Asset name (confirmed): `synthea-with-dependencies.jar`** — a fat/prebuilt JAR, ~201 MB.
- **Working download URLs (both verified — v4.0.0 returned HTTP 200, content-length 201,164,144 bytes; master-branch-latest returned a 302 to the signed asset store, i.e. valid):**
  - Pinned/reproducible (recommended for a prototype): `https://github.com/synthetichealth/synthea/releases/download/v4.0.0/synthea-with-dependencies.jar`
  - Rolling latest: `https://github.com/synthetichealth/synthea/releases/download/master-branch-latest/synthea-with-dependencies.jar`
- Auth: **No** (public GitHub release). License: **Apache-2.0**. Format: runnable Java JAR (needs Java 11+; repo targets Java 21).

### Does Synthea emit Coverage / Claim / ExplanationOfBenefit in R4? — YES
Confirmed by inspecting `src/main/java/org/mitre/synthea/export/FhirR4.java` on master: it contains `new Coverage`, an `encounterClaim(...)` builder (emits FHIR `Claim`), and 35 references to `ExplanationOfBenefit` (per-encounter EOB builder). Claim `type` includes a `pharmacy` coding, so prescription/pharmacy claims are represented. Patient, AllergyIntolerance, Condition, and MedicationRequest are core Synthea R4 outputs.

Note on mechanics: Coverage/Claim/EOB are produced **as part of the normal FHIR export** — there is no dedicated `exporter.fhir.claim=...` toggle. They appear because Synthea models payers/insurance internally (the `generate.payers.*` engine, below) and attaches costs/coverage to every encounter and medication. To get only certain resource types you filter with `exporter.fhir.included_resources` / `exporter.fhir.excluded_resources`.

### Relevant `synthea.properties` keys (quoted verbatim from master `src/main/resources/synthea.properties`)
```
exporter.fhir.export = true
exporter.fhir.use_us_core_ig = true
exporter.fhir.us_core_version = 6.1.0
exporter.fhir.transaction_bundle = true
exporter.fhir.bulk_data = false
exporter.fhir.included_resources =
exporter.fhir.excluded_resources =

generate.payers.insurance_companies.default_file = payers/insurance_companies.csv
generate.payers.insurance_plans.default_file = payers/insurance_plans.csv
generate.payers.insurance_plans.eligibilities_file = payers/insurance_eligibilities.csv
generate.payers.insurance_companies.medicare = Medicare
generate.payers.insurance_companies.medicaid = Medicaid
generate.payers.insurance_companies.dual_eligible = Dual Eligible
generate.payers.selection_behavior = priority
generate.payers.adjustment_behavior = none
generate.payers.adjustment_rate = 0.10
generate.payers.loss_of_care = false
generate.insurance.mandate.year = 2006
generate.insurance.employer_coverage = 0.83
generate.payers.insurance_plans.income_premium_ratio = 0.034
```
So payer behavior is driven by the `payers/insurance_companies.csv` and `payers/insurance_plans.csv` seed files plus the `generate.payers.*` properties; the FHIR shape of the output is controlled by the `exporter.fhir.*` block. `exporter.fhir.transaction_bundle = true` is already the default on master.

### Exact headless command to produce R4 transaction bundles
Every property can be overridden on the CLI with `--<property>=<value>`. Example that generates 1000 patients from a fixed seed, US-Core R4 transaction bundles, into a chosen directory:
```
java -jar synthea-with-dependencies.jar \
  -p 1000 -s 12345 -cs 6789 \
  --exporter.baseDirectory=./output_tx/ \
  --exporter.fhir.export=true \
  --exporter.fhir.transaction_bundle=true \
  --exporter.fhir.use_us_core_ig=true \
  Massachusetts Boston
```
CLI flags confirmed from `README.md` / `Generator.java`: `-p` population, `-s` seed, `-cs` clinician seed, `-g`/`-a` gender/age filter, trailing `[state [city]]`, `-m` module name filter, `-d` local modules dir, `-k` keep-matching-patients module. Output lands in `output/fhir/` (or your `--exporter.baseDirectory`).

### Targeting specific conditions/medications (diabetes + penicillin allergy) and biasing the population
Two complementary mechanisms, both confirmed in source:
- **`-m <module>` module filter** — restrict which disease modules run. Confirmed relevant modules in `src/main/resources/modules`: `allergies.json` (drug allergies, incl. penicillin), `food_allergies.json`, `allergic_rhinitis.json`, and the diabetes/T2D progression under `metabolic_syndrome_disease.json` + `metabolic_syndrome_care.json` (there is no standalone `diabetes.json`; diabetes is modeled inside the metabolic-syndrome modules). Example: `-m "metabolic_syndrome*:allergies"`.
- **`-k <keepModule.json>` keep-matching-patients filter** (flag `keepPatientsModulePath` in `Generator.java`) — Synthea keeps generating and **discards every patient who does not match** a supplied "keep module" (a small Generic-Module-Framework JSON whose logic tests for, e.g., an active diabetes condition AND a penicillin allergy). This is the canonical way to bias/guarantee a demo cohort toward specific drugs/allergies. The Inferno `uscore-data-script` (item 3) uses exactly this pattern.
- For medication bias you can also author/drop a custom Generic Module via `-d <localModulesDir>` that prescribes the target drug. Overriding prevalence in the base demographics is possible but heavier; the keep-module approach is the pragmatic one for a demo.

## 2. CMS synthetic claims datasets (real datasets, not generators)

### CMS DE-SynPUF (Data Entrepreneurs' Synthetic Public Use File)
- **What it is:** synthesized data from a 5% sample of 2008 Medicare beneficiaries with 2008–2010 claims. Five data types, **including Prescription Drug Events (Part D PDE)** — plus Beneficiary Summary, Inpatient, Outpatient, and Carrier claims. Distributed as 20 subsamples (~0.25% each); each subsample = 8 files (3 yearly beneficiary files, 1 inpatient, 1 outpatient, 1 PDE, 2 carrier).
- **Format:** CSV, delivered as ZIP archives (flat claims tables, **not** FHIR).
- **Auth:** **No login required** — public files on cms.gov. (Note: the CMS download pages return HTTP 403 to automated fetchers/bots but are reachable in a normal browser.)
- **License:** CMS public-use file, effectively public domain / no data-use agreement for the synthetic PUF.
- **URLs:**
  - Landing/overview: `https://www.cms.gov/data-research/statistics-trends-and-reports/medicare-claims-synthetic-public-use-files/cms-2008-2010-data-entrepreneurs-synthetic-public-use-file-de-synpuf`
  - Sample-1 download page: `.../de10-sample-1` (sample-2 … sample-20 analogously)
  - Convenience CSV mirror on GitHub (reachable from this sandbox): `https://github.com/milwaukeedata/desynpuf`
  - OMOP CDM version on AWS Open Data (no login, S3): `https://registry.opendata.aws/cmsdesynpuf-omop/`
- **Fit:** Best real source for **Part D pharmacy claim** volume/shape and adjudication fields (payment, patient-pay, ingredient cost). You'd map CSV → FHIR Claim/ClaimResponse/EOB yourself; not FHIR out of the box.

### CMS BCDA (Beneficiary Claims Data API) sandbox + Blue Button-style synthetic data
- **What it is:** BCDA sandbox serves **synthetic FHIR R4 bulk-export files** — sample **ExplanationOfBenefit, Patient, and Coverage** NDJSON (bulk-data). Synthetic records use **negative Patient IDs**.
- **Auth:** sandbox is open to anyone, **but you need a bearer token** — CMS publishes **generic sandbox client-id/secret**, so effectively no personal account needed. Downloadable **sample files are available without any token**.
- **Format:** FHIR R4 NDJSON (bulk-export). **License:** US Gov / public.
- **URLs:** sandbox `https://sandbox.bcda.cms.gov/`; docs `https://bcda.cms.gov/`, `https://bcda.cms.gov/api-documentation.html`; data page `https://bcda.cms.gov/bcda-data.html`.
- **Fit:** Closest to a ready-made FHIR **EOB + Coverage** payer dataset — ideal reference for adjudicated-claim (EOB) shapes on a HAPI server, though it lacks the request-side `Claim`/`ClaimResponse` prior-auth pair.

### HL7 Da Vinci PAS (Prior Authorization Support) example bundles — best `Claim`/`ClaimResponse` reference
- **Repo:** `https://github.com/HL7/davinci-pas` (IG source; XML/JSON example instances live in the repo and rendered IG). Reference implementation: `https://github.com/HL7-DaVinci/prior-auth`.
- **Auth:** No. **Format:** FHIR R4 XML/JSON example resources/bundles. **License:** HL7 (Creative Commons CC0 / public-domain for the IG artifacts).
- **Concrete example instances** (current IG v2.2.x): `Bundle-PASClaimInquiryResponseBundleExample`, `Bundle-ErrorResponseBundleExample`, plus Referral/Rejection/Pending response bundles and `Claim`/`ClaimResponse` profile examples — rendered at `https://build.fhir.org/ig/HL7/davinci-pas/`. PAS puts the prior-auth number in `ClaimResponse.preAuthRef`.
- **Fit:** The authoritative model for **request/response Claim ↔ ClaimResponse** shapes in an adjudication/prior-auth flow — exactly the pair BCDA/DE-SynPUF don't give you. Use these as canonical profile references for your prototype's Claim and ClaimResponse.

## 3. Other maintained open tools for synthesizing FHIR payer/claims data

- **Synthea (MITRE)** — `https://github.com/synthetichealth/synthea` — No auth, Apache-2.0, FHIR R4 JAR. The primary generator; emits Patient/Coverage/Claim/EOB/MedicationRequest/AllergyIntolerance/Condition in one run. Best all-in-one for adjudication demo data.
- **Inferno `uscore-data-script` (ONC/MITRE)** — `https://github.com/inferno-framework/uscore-data-script` — No auth, open source. Wraps Synthea + a keep-module to produce a *small, complete* US-Core cohort covering all Must-Support elements. Good for a lean demo seed rather than bulk.
- **Inferno reference server (pre-loaded US Core data)** — `https://github.com/inferno-framework/inferno-reference-server` — No auth, open source. A HAPI-like FHIR server pre-seeded with synthetic US Core data; handy to diff against your HAPI setup.
- **HL7 Da Vinci PAS / prior-auth RI** — `https://github.com/HL7/davinci-pas`, `https://github.com/HL7-DaVinci/prior-auth` — No auth, HL7/CC0. Reference Claim/ClaimResponse adjudication engine + example bundles.
- **DE-SynPUF in OMOP on AWS Open Data** — `https://registry.opendata.aws/cmsdesynpuf-omop/` — No auth (public S3). Same CMS synthetic Medicare (incl. Part D) in OMOP CDM; good if you want a relational source to ETL into FHIR.
- **Kaggle "CMS Synthetic Data" mirror** — `https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/anikannal/cms-synthetic-data` — Kaggle **account required** to download; CSV mirror of DE-SynPUF. Convenience only; prefer the CMS/GitHub/AWS sources above.

## 1. RxNorm via RxNav REST API (no UMLS license)

- **Base URL:** `https://rxnav.nlm.nih.gov/REST/` — no login, no key.
- **Format:** JSON (`.json`) or XML (`.xml`) by suffix.
- **Working calls (all verified):**
  - RxCUI by drug name: `curl "https://rxnav.nlm.nih.gov/REST/rxcui.json?name=warfarin"` → `{"idGroup":{"rxnormId":["11289"]}}`
  - Related brand/generic: `curl "https://rxnav.nlm.nih.gov/REST/rxcui/11289/related.json?tty=BN"` → returned Coumadin (202421), Jantoven (405155). Use `tty=IN` for ingredient, `tty=SCD`/`SBD` for clinical/branded drugs.
  - ATC drug class (RxClass): `curl "https://rxnav.nlm.nih.gov/REST/rxclass/class/byRxcui.json?rxcui=11289&relaSource=ATC"` → classId `B01AA` "Vitamin K antagonists".
  - VA drug class: `curl "https://rxnav.nlm.nih.gov/REST/rxclass/class/byDrugName.json?drugName=warfarin&relaSource=VA"` → classId `BL110` "ANTICOAGULANTS".
- **License/redistribution:** RxNav APIs are free/public; RxNorm content is in the public domain. No UMLS license needed to *call the API*.
- **UMLS confirmation:** The RxNorm **full monthly release** (`https://download.nlm.nih.gov/umls/kss/rxnorm/RxNorm_full_current.zip`) **does require UMLS login/API key** — confirmed on the NLM docs page. Bonus: the **RxNorm Current Prescribable Content** files are documented as "no license required" (host `download.nlm.nih.gov`, not tested for sandbox reachability).
- **Adjudication use:** Normalize the submitted NDC/drug to an ingredient RxCUI, resolve therapeutic class (ATC/VA) to drive drug-allergy and duplicate-therapy/step-therapy rules, and map brand↔generic for formulary/generic-substitution logic.

## 2. ICD-10-CM diagnosis codes in bulk (no login)

**(i) NLM Clinical Tables API** — `https://clinicaltables.nlm.nih.gov/api/icd10cm/v3/search`
- No login/key. Format: JSON array `[total, [codes], null, [[code,name],…]]`.
- Verified: `curl "https://clinicaltables.nlm.nih.gov/api/icd10cm/v3/search?sf=code,name&terms=diabetes&count=3"`
- **Paging:** use `offset` + `count`; `count`/`maxList` max = **500**; documented hard cap **offset+count ≤ 7,500**, and reported totals capped at 10,000. It is a *search/autocomplete* API (requires a `terms` filter) — good for on-demand validation, not a clean full dump. Verified paging: `...?terms=diabetes&maxList=5&offset=3&count=5&sf=code,name`.
- License: free "as is," public domain source data.

**(ii) CDC bulk order files (full code set)** — `https://ftp.cdc.gov/pub/Health_Statistics/NCHS/Publications/ICD10CM/<YEAR>/`
- No login. Directory listing verified. Current-year (FY2026) files:

  - Addenda: `.../2026/icd10cm-addenda-2026.zip`
  - (FY2025 equivalent: `.../2025/ICD10-CM%20Code%20Descriptions%202025.zip`)
- Format: ZIP of fixed-width/plain-text description files. Public domain.
- **Adjudication use:** Clinical Tables for real-time diagnosis-code validation on the claim; CDC zip to load the complete code set into a reference table for medical-necessity / diagnosis-based edits (prior-auth criteria, NCD/LCD linkage).

# Synthetic Payer/Claims FHIR Data — Prework Findings

All facts below were verified live against the GitHub API/raw source and web search on 2026-07-13.

## 1. SYNTHEA deep-dive (github.com/synthetichealth/synthea)

### Version + JAR asset (confirmed against GitHub Releases API)
- **Latest tagged release: `v4.0.0`** (published 2026-03-05). Also a rolling `master-branch-latest` (built 2026-06-30) that tracks the master branch.
- **Asset name (confirmed): `synthea-with-dependencies.jar`** — a fat/prebuilt JAR, ~201 MB.
- **Working download URLs (both verified — v4.0.0 returned HTTP 200, content-length 201,164,144 bytes; master-branch-latest returned a 302 to the signed asset store, i.e. valid):**
  - Pinned/reproducible (recommended for a prototype): `https://github.com/synthetichealth/synthea/releases/download/v4.0.0/synthea-with-dependencies.jar`
  - Rolling latest: `https://github.com/synthetichealth/synthea/releases/download/master-branch-latest/synthea-with-dependencies.jar`
- Auth: **No** (public GitHub release). License: **Apache-2.0**. Format: runnable Java JAR (needs Java 11+; repo targets Java 21).

### Does Synthea emit Coverage / Claim / ExplanationOfBenefit in R4? — YES
Confirmed by inspecting `src/main/java/org/mitre/synthea/export/FhirR4.java` on master: it contains `new Coverage`, an `encounterClaim(...)` builder (emits FHIR `Claim`), and 35 references to `ExplanationOfBenefit` (per-encounter EOB builder). Claim `type` includes a `pharmacy` coding, so prescription/pharmacy claims are represented. Patient, AllergyIntolerance, Condition, and MedicationRequest are core Synthea R4 outputs.

Note on mechanics: Coverage/Claim/EOB are produced **as part of the normal FHIR export** — there is no dedicated `exporter.fhir.claim=...` toggle. They appear because Synthea models payers/insurance internally (the `generate.payers.*` engine, below) and attaches costs/coverage to every encounter and medication. To get only certain resource types you filter with `exporter.fhir.included_resources` / `exporter.fhir.excluded_resources`.

### Relevant `synthea.properties` keys (quoted verbatim from master `src/main/resources/synthea.properties`)
```
exporter.fhir.export = true
exporter.fhir.use_us_core_ig = true
exporter.fhir.us_core_version = 6.1.0
exporter.fhir.transaction_bundle = true
exporter.fhir.bulk_data = false
exporter.fhir.included_resources =
exporter.fhir.excluded_resources =

generate.payers.insurance_companies.default_file = payers/insurance_companies.csv
generate.payers.insurance_plans.default_file = payers/insurance_plans.csv
generate.payers.insurance_plans.eligibilities_file = payers/insurance_eligibilities.csv
generate.payers.insurance_companies.medicare = Medicare
generate.payers.insurance_companies.medicaid = Medicaid
generate.payers.insurance_companies.dual_eligible = Dual Eligible
generate.payers.selection_behavior = priority
generate.payers.adjustment_behavior = none
generate.payers.adjustment_rate = 0.10
generate.payers.loss_of_care = false
generate.insurance.mandate.year = 2006
generate.insurance.employer_coverage = 0.83
generate.payers.insurance_plans.income_premium_ratio = 0.034
```
So payer behavior is driven by the `payers/insurance_companies.csv` and `payers/insurance_plans.csv` seed files plus the `generate.payers.*` properties; the FHIR shape of the output is controlled by the `exporter.fhir.*` block. `exporter.fhir.transaction_bundle = true` is already the default on master.

### Exact headless command to produce R4 transaction bundles
Every property can be overridden on the CLI with `--<property>=<value>`. Example that generates 1000 patients from a fixed seed, US-Core R4 transaction bundles, into a chosen directory:
```
java -jar synthea-with-dependencies.jar \
  -p 1000 -s 12345 -cs 6789 \
  --exporter.baseDirectory=./output_tx/ \
  --exporter.fhir.export=true \
  --exporter.fhir.transaction_bundle=true \
  --exporter.fhir.use_us_core_ig=true \
  Massachusetts Boston
```
CLI flags confirmed from `README.md` / `Generator.java`: `-p` population, `-s` seed, `-cs` clinician seed, `-g`/`-a` gender/age filter, trailing `[state [city]]`, `-m` module name filter, `-d` local modules dir, `-k` keep-matching-patients module. Output lands in `output/fhir/` (or your `--exporter.baseDirectory`).

### Targeting specific conditions/medications (diabetes + penicillin allergy) and biasing the population
Two complementary mechanisms, both confirmed in source:
- **`-m <module>` module filter** — restrict which disease modules run. Confirmed relevant modules in `src/main/resources/modules`: `allergies.json` (drug allergies, incl. penicillin), `food_allergies.json`, `allergic_rhinitis.json`, and the diabetes/T2D progression under `metabolic_syndrome_disease.json` + `metabolic_syndrome_care.json` (there is no standalone `diabetes.json`; diabetes is modeled inside the metabolic-syndrome modules). Example: `-m "metabolic_syndrome*:allergies"`.
- **`-k <keepModule.json>` keep-matching-patients filter** (flag `keepPatientsModulePath` in `Generator.java`) — Synthea keeps generating and **discards every patient who does not match** a supplied "keep module" (a small Generic-Module-Framework JSON whose logic tests for, e.g., an active diabetes condition AND a penicillin allergy). This is the canonical way to bias/guarantee a demo cohort toward specific drugs/allergies. The Inferno `uscore-data-script` (item 3) uses exactly this pattern.
- For medication bias you can also author/drop a custom Generic Module via `-d <localModulesDir>` that prescribes the target drug. Overriding prevalence in the base demographics is possible but heavier; the keep-module approach is the pragmatic one for a demo.

## 2. CMS synthetic claims datasets (real datasets, not generators)

### CMS DE-SynPUF (Data Entrepreneurs' Synthetic Public Use File)
- **What it is:** synthesized data from a 5% sample of 2008 Medicare beneficiaries with 2008–2010 claims. Five data types, **including Prescription Drug Events (Part D PDE)** — plus Beneficiary Summary, Inpatient, Outpatient, and Carrier claims. Distributed as 20 subsamples (~0.25% each); each subsample = 8 files (3 yearly beneficiary files, 1 inpatient, 1 outpatient, 1 PDE, 2 carrier).
- **Format:** CSV, delivered as ZIP archives (flat claims tables, **not** FHIR).
- **Auth:** **No login required** — public files on cms.gov. (Note: the CMS download pages return HTTP 403 to automated fetchers/bots but are reachable in a normal browser.)
- **License:** CMS public-use file, effectively public domain / no data-use agreement for the synthetic PUF.
- **URLs:**
  - Landing/overview: `https://www.cms.gov/data-research/statistics-trends-and-reports/medicare-claims-synthetic-public-use-files/cms-2008-2010-data-entrepreneurs-synthetic-public-use-file-de-synpuf`
  - Sample-1 download page: `.../de10-sample-1` (sample-2 … sample-20 analogously)
  - Convenience CSV mirror on GitHub (reachable from this sandbox): `https://github.com/milwaukeedata/desynpuf`
  - OMOP CDM version on AWS Open Data (no login, S3): `https://registry.opendata.aws/cmsdesynpuf-omop/`
- **Fit:** Best real source for **Part D pharmacy claim** volume/shape and adjudication fields (payment, patient-pay, ingredient cost). You'd map CSV → FHIR Claim/ClaimResponse/EOB yourself; not FHIR out of the box.

Confirmed by inspecting `src/main/java/org/mitre/synthea/export/FhirR4.java` on master: it contains `new Coverage`, an `encounterClaim(...)` builder (emits FHIR `Claim`), and 35 references to `ExplanationOfBenefit` (per-encounter EOB builder). exporter.fhir.use_us_core_ig = true
```
exporter.fhir.us_core_version = 6.1.0
exporter.fhir.transaction_bundle = true
exporter.fhir.bulk_data = false
exporter.fhir.included_resources =
exporter.fhir.excluded_resources =

generate.payers.insurance_companies.default_file = payers/insurance_companies.csv
generate.payers.insurance_plans.default_file = payers/insurance_plans.csv
generate.payers.insurance_plans.eligibilities_file = payers/insurance_eligibilities.csv
generate.payers.insurance_companies.medicare = Medicare
generate.payers.insurance_companies.medicaid = Medicaid
generate.payers.insurance_companies.dual_eligible = Dual Eligible
generate.payers.selection_behavior = priority
generate.payers.adjustment_behavior = none
generate.payers.adjustment_rate = 0.10
generate.payers.loss_of_care = false
generate.insurance.mandate.year = 2006
generate.insurance.employer_coverage = 0.83
generate.payers.insurance_plans.income_premium_ratio = 0.034
```
So payer behavior is driven by the `payers/insurance_companies.csv` and `payers/insurance_plans.csv` seed files plus the `generate.payers.*` properties; the FHIR shape of the output is controlled by the `exporter.fhir.*` block. `exporter.fhir.transaction_bundle = true` is already the default on master.

### Exact headless command to produce R4 transaction bundles
Every property can be overridden on the CLI with `--<property>=<value>`. Example that generates 1000 patients from a fixed seed, US-Core R4 transaction bundles, into a chosen directory:
```
java -jar synthea-with-dependencies.jar \
  -p 1000 -s 12345 -cs 6789 \
  --exporter.baseDirectory=./output_tx/ \
  --exporter.fhir.export=true \
  --exporter.fhir.transaction_bundle=true \
  --exporter.fhir.use_us_core_ig=true \
  Massachusetts Boston
```
CLI flags confirmed from `README.md` / `Generator.java`: `-p` population, `-s` seed, `-cs` clinician seed, `-g`/`-a` gender/age filter, trailing `[state [city]]`, `-m` module name filter, `-d` local modules dir, `-k` keep-matching-patients module. Output lands in `output/fhir/` (or your `--exporter.baseDirectory`).

Two complementary mechanisms, both confirmed in source:

Confirmed relevant modules in `src/main/resources/modules`: `allergies.json` (drug allergies, incl. penicillin), `food_allergies.json`, `allergic_rhinitis.json`, and the diabetes/T2D progression under `metabolic_syndrome_disease.json` + `metabolic_syndrome_care.json` (there is no standalone `diabetes.json`; diabetes is modeled inside the metabolic-syndrome modules). # Phase 2 — Reference & Synthetic Data (data-engineering prework)

> **Not part of the documentation PR.** This lives on the local `dataeng/phase2-prework`
> branch. Raw downloads (Synthea jar, CMS zips, formulary PUF) are **gitignored**;
> only small, public-domain, curated derivatives and this README are tracked.
> Everything here is reproducible from the scripts noted below.
>
> All sources verified reachable & **no-auth** from this environment on 2026-07-13.

## TL;DR — what to use for the adjudication demo

- **Synthesize patients/claims:** Synthea v4.0.0 JAR → Patient, Condition, MedicationRequest,
  AllergyIntolerance, **Claim**, **ExplanationOfBenefit** (validated: 657 Claim + 657 EOB from a
  p=3 run). Bias the cohort with a `-k` keep-module (diabetes + penicillin allergy).
- **Formulary/PA/step-therapy/quantity rules (REAL):** CMS Medicare Part D Formulary PUF (per-NDC
  tier + PA + ST + QL flags). 2.4 GB — URL documented; pull a slice when needed.
- **Drug normalization & class:** RxNav REST API (RxCUI + ATC/VA class) — no download needed.
- **Diagnoses:** NLM Clinical Tables API (on-demand validation) + CDC full ICD-10-CM zip.
- **Medical-necessity rules:** CMS NCD export (downloaded).
- **Provider eligibility:** NPPES NPI API.
- **Canonical Claim/ClaimResponse shape:** HL7 Da Vinci PAS IG (reference) + local Synthea samples.

## Inventory

| Source | Status | Location / URL | Auth | License | Adjudication use |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Synthea v4.0.0 JAR** | ✅ downloaded (188 MB, gitignored) | `data/synthea/synthea-with-dependencies.jar` · `github.com/synthetichealth/synthea/releases/download/v4.0.0/synthea-with-dependencies.jar` | none | Apache-2.0 | Generate Patient/Condition/MedicationRequest/AllergyIntolerance/Claim/EOB transaction bundles |
| **Synthea sample output** | ✅ generated (p=3, gitignored) | `data/synthea/output/fhir/` | — | Apache-2.0 (synthetic) | Validated payer/claims emission |
| **RxNorm / RxClass** | ✅ derivative pulled | `rxnorm/rxnorm_drug_classes.csv` (20 drugs, real RxCUI + ATC) · `rxnav.nlm.nih.gov/REST/` | none | Public domain | Normalize drug→RxCUI→ATC class for drug-allergy, duplicate/step-therapy, formulary |
| **ICD-10-CM** | ✅ derivative pulled | `icd10/icd10cm_subset.csv` (153 codes) · full set: `ftp.cdc.gov/.../ICD10CM/2026/icd10cm-Code Descriptions-2026.zip` | none | Public domain | Diagnosis validation, coding-coherence & medical-necessity edits |
| **CMS NCD export** | ✅ downloaded (gitignored) | `cms-ncd/ncd.mdb`, `ncd_csv.zip` · `downloads.cms.gov/medicare-coverage-database/downloads/exports/ncd.zip` | none | US Gov / public domain | Medical-necessity (Layer-1 federal rules) |
| **CMS Part D Formulary PUF** | ⏳ referenced (2.4 GB) | `data.cms.gov/sites/default/files/2026-04/65e8dafd-c42b-4c2a-93c2-551bbc80bef9/SPUF_2026_20260408.zip` | none | US Gov / public domain | **Real** per-NDC formulary status, tier, PA, step-therapy, quantity-limit flags |
| **NPPES NPI** | ⏳ referenced (API) | `npiregistry.cms.hhs.gov/api/?version=2.1` · bulk: `download.cms.gov/nppes/NPPES_Data_Dissemination_July_2026_V2.zip` | none | Public / FOIA | Prescriber & pharmacy eligibility/taxonomy/active-status |
| **openFDA NDC/label** | ⏳ referenced (API) | `api.fda.gov/drug/ndc.json`, `api.fda.gov/drug/label.json` | none (key optional) | CC0-ish | NDC↔product resolution, labeling/contraindication signals |
| **Local Claim/EOB samples** | ✅ extracted | `samples/example_pharmacy_claim.json`, `samples/example_eob.json` | — | Apache-2.0 (synthetic) | Canonical `Claim`(type=pharmacy)/EOB shapes for our FHIR artefacts |
| **HL7 Da Vinci PAS** | ⏳ referenced | `build.fhir.org/ig/HL7/davinci-pas/` · `github.com/HL7/davinci-pas` | none | HL7 CC0 | Canonical request/response `Claim`↔`ClaimResponse` (PA number in `ClaimResponse.preAuthRef`) |
| **CMS DE-SynPUF** | ⏳ referenced | `www.cms.gov/.../de-synpuf`; OMOP on AWS Open Data `registry.opendata.aws/cmsdesynpuf-omop/` | none (CMS pages 403 bots) | Public domain | Real Part D pharmacy-claim field distributions (CSV → map to FHIR) |
| **CMS BCDA sandbox** | ⏳ referenced | `sandbox.bcda.cms.gov/`, `bcda.cms.gov/bcda-data.html` | generic token | US Gov | Synthetic FHIR EOB/Coverage NDJSON reference |

Legend: ✅ obtained locally · ⏳ verified + documented, pull on demand.

## Reproduce

```bash
# Small reference derivatives (ICD-10 subset + RxNorm/ATC classes):
python3 data/scripts/fetch_reference_data.py

# Synthea generator (already fetched to data/synthea/, gitignored):
#   curl -sL -o data/synthea/synthea-with-dependencies.jar \
#     https://github.com/synthetichealth/synthea/releases/download/v4.0.0/synthea-with-dependencies.jar

# Generate a claims-bearing R4 population (transaction bundles → loadable into HAPI):
java -jar data/synthea/synthea-with-dependencies.jar \
  -p 10 -s 20260713 \
  --exporter.baseDirectory data/synthea/output \
  --exporter.fhir.transaction_bundle true \
  Massachusetts
```

## Notes & caveats

- **Coverage not in default Synthea R4 export.** The p=3 run emitted Claim/EOB/Provenance/Organization
  but **no `Coverage`**. Synthea models payers internally; Coverage appears via the payer/US-Core
  config. For the demo we will **author `Coverage` in the claims seed** (grounded to our plan
  definitions), as `seed_demo.py` already does for its resources — don't assume Synthea provides it.
- **Part D Formulary PUF is 2.4 GB.** Don't commit or bulk-load it. When needed, download once,
  extract only the Basic-Drugs-Formulary table, and distill a **curated** subset into `data/payer-kb/`
  (Phase 2 plan M1). This keeps us within the "curated fixtures" requirement (R13) and avoids the
  AMA/CPT redistribution concern.
- **CMS HTML pages 403 automated fetchers** but the underlying files on `data.cms.gov` / `downloads.cms.gov`
  download fine (verified). `synthea.mitre.org` is unreachable here — use the GitHub JAR.
- **RxNorm full monthly release** needs a UMLS login; we deliberately use the **no-auth RxNav API**
  instead, which is sufficient for RxCUI + class resolution.

content.text:
Part 1 (data prework) is **done and committed to the local `dataeng/phase2-prework` branch — not pushed, entirely off the docs PR**, as you required. Summary before I move to the cloud thinking:

**Data prework results**
- **Synthesis tool secured & validated:** Synthea v4.0.0 JAR (188MB, gitignored) — confirmed it emits **657 `Claim` + 657 `ExplanationOfBenefit`** plus Patient/Condition/MedicationRequest/AllergyIntolerance in one run. Cohort can be biased to "diabetes + penicillin allergy" via a `-k` keep-module.
- **Real reference data pulled (no-auth):** 153 ICD-10-CM codes (NLM), 20 drugs with real RxCUIs + ATC classes (RxNav — the ATC groupings ground our duplicate-therapy/formulary rules), CMS NCD export (medical-necessity), and real pharmacy `Claim`/`EOB` samples extracted from Synthea.
- **The jackpot source, documented for on-demand pull:** the **CMS Part D Formulary PUF** has *real per-NDC tier / prior-auth / step-therapy / quantity-limit flags* — exactly our rule inputs (2.4GB, so URL documented, not bulk-loaded; we distill a curated slice into `data/payer-kb/` per R13).
- Full inventory + licenses + reproduce commands in `data/reference/README.md`; a `Coverage`-not-in-default-Synthea gotcha is flagged (we author Coverage in the seed).

---

Now **parts 2 & 3 — cloud security, observability, deployability, and scalability.** This is genuinely architectural and touches the requirements, so let me brainstorm before writing anything into the docs.

## Security (treat claims data as if it were PHI)

- **🔴 Concrete finding in existing config:** Kong's `file-log` plugin logs `request.uri` (e.g. `/fhir/Patient/123`) to stdout → **patient identifiers land in Cloud Logging**. For claims/PHI that's a leak. Fix: scrub identifiers or treat logs as a PHI store (restricted, retention-limited). This exists in Phase 1 today.
- **AuthN depth:** Kong static API keys = coarse identity. Claims adjudication has distinct roles (submitter, reviewer, agent). The healthcare-standard answer is **OAuth2/OIDC + scopes (SMART-on-FHIR)** via Kong's OIDC plugin — the clinical client README already anticipates this migration. Fork: keep API keys for the prototype vs introduce JWT/OIDC now.
- **Secrets:** move from imperative k8s Secrets → **GCP Secret Manager + Workload Identity** (rotation, no base64-in-etcd). Managed, scalable, matches the "managed services" directive.
- **Data protection:** TLS everywhere incl. the Kong proxy (currently no TLS — README known-limitation), encryption at rest (Neon/Cloud SQL), parameterized queries in the "SQL400-like" emulator tables (injection surface), and the anti-corruption layer doubles as the input-validation boundary.
- Non-repudiation is already strong (Provenance per decision + gateway audit log).

## Observability

- **Distributed tracing is the big gap.** One claim fans out to emulator + triage + fhir; without trace propagation you can't see a single adjudication end-to-end. Recommend **OpenTelemetry** (W3C `traceparent`) across services → **Cloud Trace**; Kong's OTel plugin propagates at the edge.
- **Metrics:** Micrometer→Prometheus (Spring), Prometheus (FastAPI) → **Google Managed Prometheus** (already declared in `kong-values.yaml`). Emit *business* metrics: approvals/denials/pends, rule-fire counts, per-stage latency.
- **Correlation IDs** in structured logs (PHI-scrubbed), and a **decisions dashboard** off the audit trail — a great Lead-Director demo artifact.

## Deployability

- Everything is already container-first. The gap is **imperative bash (`deploy.sh`)**. The devcontainer already ships Terraform — recommend **Terraform for GCP infra** (GKE/Cloud Run, Cloud SQL, Secret Manager, Artifact Registry, networking) + **GitHub Actions CI/CD** (build → vuln-scan → push → deploy). This makes "easily deployable + reproducible" real.

## Scalability (this is where your directive reshapes the architecture)

Your "containers or GCP lambda-equivalent + managed scalable data" pushes toward a cleaner target than Phase 1's GKE-only:

- **Compute:** the new services (claims-service, legacy-emulator, triage, claims-agent) are **stateless request/response** → ideal **Cloud Run** (GCP's serverless-containers = the "lambda equivalent"; scale-to-zero, autoscale on concurrency). **Exception: HAPI FHIR** has a ~3-min cold start (see the 180s k8s probe) — keep it always-on (Cloud Run `min-instances≥1` or a GKE Deployment). Spring cold-start is mitigated with min-instances / GraalVM native.
- **A bonus this unlocks:** if services run on Cloud Run, run **DB-less declarative Kong as the edge in *both* local and cloud** (fronting Cloud Run URLs in cloud, containers locally). That uses **one Kong config dialect everywhere** — which *eliminates the KIC-vs-`kong.yml` drift risk* I flagged in the plan. Nice convergence.
- **Data — mapping to your NoSQL/sharded prompt:**
  - **FHIR** → Postgres (Neon already autoscales like Aurora Serverless; scale via the `-pooler` + read replicas; HAPI supports partitioning / Elasticsearch for search at high scale).
  - **Formulary / PA rules** → this is the canonical **high-cardinality key-value** workload (`plan_id + NDC → rule`). Full Part D is millions of rows → the right scale answer is **Bigtable or Firestore** (GCP's DynamoDB/wide-column equivalents), *not* relational. This is exactly your "non-relational" instinct.
  - **Decision audit** → append-only, high-volume → stream to **BigQuery** for the audit warehouse + rule analytics (also powers the observability dashboard).
  - **Caching / rate-limit at scale** → **Memorystore (Redis)** (Kong's `redis` policy — README already notes this upgrade path).
- **Scale pattern:** keep the prototype small (R13 curated data), but put formulary behind a **repository interface** so Postgres→Bigtable is a swap, and make claim intake **Pub/Sub-ready** (accept→enqueue→adjudicate) so bursts decouple. Build small; make the scale path obvious — the right story for a Lead-Director prototype.

### R13 — Reference data hygiene
Use **curated fixtures** (small RxNorm/ICD subset, formulary, PA rules, 4 plan
definitions) checked into a `data/payer-kb/` folder; **check existing FHIR data
first** before seeding. No full terminology loads. No AMA-licensed CPT beyond the
tiny curated sample. Sources are confirmed (RxNav, NLM/CDC ICD-10, CMS Part D
Formulary PUF, Synthea) and captured in the data-engineering prework (`data/reference/README.md`
on the local `dataeng/phase2-prework` branch — kept off this docs PR).

### R14 — Security & privacy (treat claims data as if PHI)
- **PHI-safe logging:** do not emit patient/member identifiers to logs. (Fix the
  existing Kong `file-log` behaviour that logs `request.uri` such as `/fhir/Patient/123`;
  scrub identifiers or treat those logs as a restricted PHI store.)
- **AuthN/Z:** static Kong API keys are acceptable for the prototype, but design for
  **OAuth2/OIDC + scopes (SMART-on-FHIR)** as the path (Kong OIDC plugin; the clinical
  client already anticipates OAuth). Consumers are least-privilege.
- **Secrets:** managed via **GCP Secret Manager + Workload Identity** in cloud (no
  secrets in git or plain k8s Secrets); local uses `.env` as today.
- **In transit / at rest:** TLS everywhere **including the gateway proxy** (close the
  Phase 1 no-TLS-on-proxy gap); encryption at rest on all managed data stores.
- **Injection safety:** the legacy emulator's SQL/400-style tables use parameterized
  queries; the anti-corruption layer is the input-validation boundary.
- **Supply chain:** container image vulnerability scanning before deploy.

### R15 — Observability
- **Distributed tracing** across the adjudication fan-out (claims → emulator + triage
  + fhir) via **OpenTelemetry** (W3C `traceparent`) → Cloud Trace; Kong propagates at
  the edge. One claim = one trace.
- **Metrics** via Micrometer/Prometheus (Java) and Prometheus (Python) → Google
  Managed Prometheus (already declared in `kong-values.yaml`): per-stage latency,
  and business metrics (approvals/denials/pends, rule-fire counts).
- **Correlation IDs** in PHI-scrubbed structured logs; health/readiness endpoints on
  every new service.

### R16 — Deployability
- **Container-first**: every service is a container, runnable locally via Compose and
  deployable to cloud with config-only differences.
- **IaC + CI/CD** for the (deferred) cloud phase: **Terraform** for GCP infra
  (Cloud Run, Cloud SQL/Neon, Secret Manager, Artifact Registry, networking) and
  **GitHub Actions** (build → scan → push → deploy). Supersedes hand-run bash.

83	### Known parity friction (tracked, not hidden)
84	Kong is configured two ways — **KIC CRDs** (cloud) and a **declarative `kong.yml`**
85	(local DB-less). They express the same 3 routes + 4 plugins in different dialects.
86	Mitigation: keep both (small) and add a test asserting they define the same
87	routes/plugins. Single source of truth via `deck` is a later option.
88

90	- Local Kong **admin** must not use `:8001` (taken by `triage`); map to `:8081`.
91	  Proxy stays `:8000` to match the cloud port-forward convention.

93	## 4. Isolation strategy (enforcing R9)
94	
95	The dependency arrow points **Phase 2 → Phase 1 only**.
96	
97	| Shared surface | How Phase 1 stays independent |
98	|---|---|
99	| `docker-compose.yml` | New services carry `profiles: [phase2]` / `[gateway]`; Phase 1 services get no profile → plain `up` is byte-for-byte today's. Verify with `docker compose config`. |
100	| Cloud deploy | `deploy.sh` and `gateway/kong/*` untouched. Phase 2 routes/manifests live in new files (`gateway/kong/phase2/`, a future `deploy-phase2.sh`). |
101	| Tests | Phase 2 tests in new packages; CI keeps a "Phase 1 only" job. `pytest.ini` extended, never narrowed. |
102	| Seeding | New `data/scripts/seed_claims_demo.py` + `data/payer-kb/`; `seed_demo.py` untouched. Use `FHIR_GATEWAY_URL` (consistency with seed_demo/agent). |
103	| `client/clinical` | Additive methods only (e.g. `get_coverage`) following the `_parse_*` pattern; no existing signature changes. Java services use their own FHIR access. |
104	| `mcp-agent` | Untouched — claims explanation is a **separate** `claims-agent` (D3). |
105	| `.ona/automations.yaml` | Append new Python pkgs to the `installDependencies` `pip install -e` list; add build tasks with `dependsOn: installDependencies`. Don't replace. |
106	
107	**Safety net:** tag `phase1-v1` (pushed) = known-good, independently deployable snapshot.
108	
109	## 5. k8s pattern for new services (deferred to Phase 2 cloud)

## 5. Cloud architecture — compute, data, security, observability, scalability

> Build is **deferred** (Phase 2 is local-first, per D8), but these decisions shape
> how we write the services now (stateless, 12-factor, repository abstractions) so the
> cloud path is a config change, not a rewrite. Decisions from the security/scalability
> brainstorm are tagged **C1–C4**.

### C1 — Compute: Cloud Run for stateless services, HAPI always-on
The new services (`claims-service`, `rxclaim-emulator`, `triage`, `claims-agent`) are
**stateless request/response** → **Cloud Run** (GCP's serverless-containers; scale-to-zero,
autoscale on concurrency, per-request billing). **HAPI FHIR stays always-on** (Cloud Run
`min-instances ≥ 1`, or a GKE Deployment) because of its ~3-min cold start (the 180s k8s
probe today). Spring cold-start is mitigated with `min-instances` and, if needed, GraalVM
native / CRaC. Privacy of the legacy core is enforced with Cloud Run **`ingress=internal`**
(+ VPC connector / IAM invoker) — the Cloud Run equivalent of the ClusterIP + NetworkPolicy
rule; **no gateway route** to the emulator.

### C2 — Gateway: DB-less Kong everywhere
One declarative `kong.yml` fronts everything in **both** environments (Cloud Run URLs as
upstreams in cloud; containers locally). Single config dialect → no drift (see §3). Kong
itself runs as a container (Cloud Run `min-instances ≥ 1`, or small GKE). Edge routes:
`/claims`, `/fhir`, `/triage`; emulator has none.

### C3 — Data: managed, scalable, with a documented NoSQL path
| Data | Store (now) | Scale path |
|---|---|---|
| FHIR resources | Postgres (Neon, autoscaling + `-pooler`) | read replicas; HAPI partitioning / Elasticsearch search |
| Formulary / PA rules | **Postgres behind a repository interface** | swap to **Bigtable/Firestore** (key: `plan_id+NDC → rule`) — the true high-cardinality KV pattern |
| Legacy emulator tables | Postgres (SQL/400-style) | small/reference; stays relational |
| Decision audit | **FHIR `Provenance`/`RiskAssessment`** in HAPI | add a **BigQuery** analytics plane later (C4) |

The repository interface for formulary/PA is the key seam: build on Postgres now, make
Bigtable/Firestore a swap, never a rewrite. Claim intake is written **Pub/Sub-ready**
(accept → enqueue → adjudicate) so bursts decouple; caching/rate-limit scale via
Memorystore (Redis) — Kong's documented `redis` policy upgrade.

### C4 — Audit/analytics: FHIR Provenance now, BigQuery later
Every decision persists a FHIR `Provenance` (as planned). A scalable BigQuery
decision-warehouse + rule-fire dashboard is **deferred** to the cloud phase.

### Security (R14) & observability (R15) in cloud
- **Secrets** → GCP Secret Manager + Workload Identity. **TLS** terminated at the edge
  incl. the proxy. **PHI-safe logging** — scrub identifiers (fixes the Kong `file-log`
  URI leak). **AuthN** stays API-key for the prototype, OIDC/JWT the documented path.
- **Tracing** → OpenTelemetry (`traceparent`) across the fan-out → Cloud Trace; **metrics**
  → Managed Prometheus (per-stage latency + approvals/denials/pends/rule-fires).
- **IaC/CI-CD (R16)** → Terraform (Cloud Run, Cloud SQL/Neon, Secret Manager, Artifact
  Registry, networking) + GitHub Actions (build → scan → push → deploy).

*(If instead we keep GKE: mirror `fhir-service/k8s/` per service — namespace labelled
`app.kubernetes.io/managed-by: kong`, ClusterIP `service`, `deployment` with
`IMAGE_PLACEHOLDER`, actuator probes; emulator = ClusterIP + NetworkPolicy. The C1
decision chose Cloud Run, so this is the fallback pattern only.)*

# Phase 2 — Claims Adjudication Modernisation Slice

> **Status: PLANNING — no application code yet.** These documents capture the
> requirements and implementation plan **we actually agreed to build**, which
> deviate in places from the source PRD (*Prescription Claim Adjudication
> Modernization Platform — Phase 2 Scope*, DRAFT). Deviations are listed
> explicitly in [`requirements.md`](./requirements.md#deviations-from-the-prd).

## What Phase 2 is

Extend the existing Phase 1 platform (prescription **refill risk triage**) into a
**prescription claim adjudication** slice: submit a claim → adjudicate it against
a simulated legacy core + deterministic benefit/prior-auth rules + reused clinical
safety checks → emit auditable FHIR decision artefacts → explain the outcome in
plain language via a dedicated agent.

Full descriptive name (from the PRD): *"Prescription Claim Adjudication
Modernisation Slice: API façade + rules service + audit trail + MCP explanation
layer."*

|---|---|
| Rules stack | **Hybrid** — Java/Spring Boot façade + legacy emulator + anti-corruption layer; **reuse** the existing Python triage service for clinical safety (drug-allergy / duplicate-therapy) |

| Legacy emulator realism | **Convincing legacy shape** (DDS-style records, DB2/SQL400 table naming, RPG/CL-flavoured adjudication function) |
| FHIR ambition | **Da Vinci-aware but generic** R4 resources (not full PAS conformance) |

(commit `d4cd4be`). See [`requirements.md` §R9](./requirements.md#r9--phase-1-independence-hard-constraint).

Derived from the DRAFT PRD plus a design conversation that adapted it to this

My review of the documents (intended for you to critique and discuss with me, not at all to blindly accept so dont change anything yet):

1. Critical: Gateway target architecture is internally contradictory, so implementation could head in two incompatible directions.
Evidence: requirements.md:109 says cloud continues existing KIC/Helm Kong, while plan.md:85, plan.md:128, and plan.md:190 define DB-less Kong everywhere with one kong.yml as source of truth.
Risk: Teams can build different gateway models and both claim compliance with docs.
Recommendation: Pick one canonical cloud gateway model for Phase 2 and add an explicit migration path section (state transition, rollback, and ownership).

2. High: Cloud isolation model for the legacy emulator is inconsistent across docs.
Evidence: requirements.md:115 specifies NetworkPolicy enforcement in cloud, but plan.md:124 specifies Cloud Run internal ingress + IAM as the control plane.
Risk: Security controls and deployment artifacts will diverge (Kubernetes policy vs Cloud Run IAM model).
Recommendation: Split requirements into “if GKE” and “if Cloud Run” controls, or lock one compute target. Or just clarify where GKE will be used and where Cloud Run will be used very, very clearly and justify.

3. High: “Committed local-only dev key” is a security bad practice, even for prototype docs.
Evidence: requirements.md:108, plan.md:79.
Risk: Secret leakage, scanner noise, accidental reuse beyond local, and normalization of insecure patterns.
Recommendation: Replace with generated-at-startup dev credentials (scripted bootstrap) and keep secrets out of git.

4. Medium: Local-first scope is clear, but the plan still embeds substantial cloud implementation detail that can blur execution focus or dissappoint stakeholders.
Evidence: requirements.md:169 says cloud deployment is out of scope now, while plan.md:111 and plan.md:177 provide deep cloud design and a full cloud milestone.
Risk: Scope mismatch and underestimation during “planning-only” phase.
Recommendation: Be very clear what cloud related work, including stubbing and testing, will be done in each milestone. For an actual deliverable, highlight the full cloud deployment and testing to a separate milestone , perhaps sometime after M7.

5. Medium: Deterministic adjudication behavior is underspecified at the contract level.
Evidence: Rules/pipeline are described, but no canonical request/response schema, error taxonomy, or rule-precedence conflict resolution in requirements.md:25, requirements.md:54, and plan.md:49.
Risk: Different implementations can produce different outcomes for the same claim.
Recommendation: Add a “Decision Contract” section with precedence matrix, deterministic tie-break rules, and example payloads.

6. Medium: Audit trail requirements are strong conceptually but missing explicit referential invariants.
Evidence: Resource list in requirements.md:63 and provenance statement in requirements.md:118 do not define mandatory links among Claim, ClaimResponse, Task, RiskAssessment, Provenance.
Risk: Partial traceability and hard-to-audit chains in demos and later productionization.
Recommendation: Specify minimum linkage rules (for example: one decision id per adjudication, mandatory references, and idempotency behavior). Idempotency is important wherever it applies, by the way whether in requirements or design. Check that thoroughly because I did not.

7. Low: Archived PRD includes command patterns likely to mislead if copied directly.
Evidence: source-prd.md:353 through source-prd.md:371 mixes gateway key setup language but uses Authorization Bearer in examples.
Risk: Reader confusion during manual validation.
Recommendation: Add a short “archived, not executable as-is” warning block near command sections or a pointer to authoritative runbooks.

8. Critical: Test strategy is present but not complete enough for deterministic adjudication confidence.
Evidence: plan.md:176 says “per-service tests” but does not define contract tests, golden fixtures governance, or replay/idempotency checks.
Risk: Regression detection gaps when rule catalog expands.
Recommendation: Add a minimum test matrix: API contract tests, rules golden tests, end-to-end golden paths, and non-regression snapshot tests.

One more point: I know the source-prd.md is intentionally archival and non-normative, but it still needs stronger “do not execute directly, has been replaced by other requirements documents” guidance to avoid misuse.

content.text:
Confirmed all eight against the live text — your evidence holds, and a couple go deeper than stated. Here's my honest critique, point by point, with where I'd push back or extend. **I've changed nothing.**

## Synthesis first
Five of your eight (1, 2, 5, 6, 8) share one root cause: the docs are strong on **architecture and isolation** but thin on the **normative contract layer** — decision semantics, referential/idempotency invariants, a single canonical gateway model, and a test matrix that enforces determinism. The framing decisions (D1–D8) and cloud decisions (C1–C4) were layered on over time without a reconciliation pass, which is exactly how R10 and C2 ended up contradicting each other. So beyond fixing each item, I'd add a short **"Decision Contract"** section as the normative anchor. I'd also **raise 5 and 6 to Critical** (they're the determinism core), leaving your other severities as-is.

## Point-by-point

**1. Gateway contradiction — agree, Critical, and it's deeper than a doc mismatch.**
Confirmed: [requirements.md:109](docs/phase2/requirements.md#L109) ("Cloud continues to use the existing KIC/Helm Kong") flatly contradicts C2 at [plan.md:128](docs/phase2/plan.md#L128)/[190](docs/phase2/plan.md#L190). But the real tension is one layer down: "Phase 1 cloud stays untouched" (KIC Kong) **plus** "DB-less Kong everywhere" implies **two Kongs in cloud**. That's not "one source of truth." The honest resolution is a **gateway strangler**: DB-less Kong is the canonical Phase 2 gateway; Phase 1's KIC Kong keeps serving `/fhir` untouched *until* an explicit, reversible migration step folds `/fhir` onto the DB-less Kong (rollback = re-point to KIC). I fully agree with your recommendation and would add that migration/rollback/ownership subsection you asked for. This is the top fix.

**2. Emulator isolation inconsistency — agree, High; also an *intra*-plan conflict.**
It's worse than requirements-vs-plan: the plan contradicts *itself* — [plan.md:66](docs/phase2/plan.md#L66) says NetworkPolicy while [plan.md:124](docs/phase2/plan.md#L124) says Cloud Run `ingress=internal`. Since C1 already **chose Cloud Run**, my recommendation over yours: don't split into "if GKE / if Cloud Run" as co-equal — that re-opens a decision we closed. Make **Cloud Run controls normative** (internal ingress + IAM invoker + VPC connector), and demote GKE/NetworkPolicy to a single clearly-labeled "fallback only" line. One canonical target, not two maintained control models. Requirements [line 115](docs/phase2/requirements.md#L115) should stop asserting NetworkPolicy as *the* control.

**3. Committed dev key — agree, and the repo makes it worse than you said.**
Confirmed at [requirements.md:108](docs/phase2/requirements.md#L108) and [plan.md:79](docs/phase2/plan.md#L79). Reinforcing evidence: this repo already runs **gitleaks** (`.github/workflows/secret-scan.yml`, commit `dd2729c` "stop writing secrets to files"). A committed key would trip the scanner or need an allowlist — actively normalizing the pattern the repo just removed. Agree with generated-at-startup. My one constraint on the fix: **preserve the zero-setup property** (the whole reason the key existed). A compose entrypoint that generates a key and templates it into both `kong.yml` and the client env at `docker compose up` keeps it one-command *and* keeps secrets out of git. So: adopt your recommendation, but the acceptance criterion is "still zero manual steps."

**4. Local-first vs deep cloud detail — partial pushback.**
I'd resist framing this as scope bloat, because the cloud depth exists *by your explicit request* (parts 2 & 3) and it's audience-relevant for a Lead-Director artifact. Also M8 is *already* fenced as `*(later)*` ([plan.md:177](docs/phase2/plan.md#L177)). So I don't want to move or thin the design — I want to **label** it better: (a) add a per-milestone "cloud touchpoint" column distinguishing *design-now/shape-the-code* work (stateless services, the C3 repository seam — these live in M2–M5) from *build-later* work; (b) rename M8 to read as a distinct deliverable phase (e.g., "Phase 2b — Cloud") with its own DoD. That addresses the stakeholder-expectation risk without discarding valuable design. Agree on the goal, disagree on "move the detail out."

**5. Decision contract underspecified — agree, and I'd raise to Critical. This is the biggest technical gap.**
The crux you're circling: **adjudication is not the triage engine's "first-match-wins."** Triage returns one `RuleResult` and stops. But a claim can fail eligibility *and* formulary *and* PA simultaneously — the PRD §9.4 example literally aggregates multiple reasons into one denial. So Phase 2 needs an **accumulate-then-resolve** model, not first-match. The contract must define:
- **Outcome precedence** (e.g., hard-reject > pend/route-to-review > approve) and how multiple denial reasons aggregate onto one `ClaimResponse`.
- **The triage→adjudication mapping** — currently undefined: does a triage `HIGH` force reject or pend? `MODERATE` → route-to-review? This is a real hole in the reuse boundary (D1).
- **Canonical request/response schemas** (we can ground these in the Da Vinci PAS shapes + the real Synthea `Claim`/`EOB` samples the prework already pulled) and an **error taxonomy** (validation error vs adjudication denial vs system error — very different HTTP/outcome semantics).
Strong agree; I'd make this the normative anchor section.

**6. Referential invariants + idempotency — agree, Critical; and I verified your suspicion.**
I grepped: **"idempoten" appears nowhere in `docs/phase2/`.** You were right to flag it as unchecked. It matters in at least four places, and they're distinct:
- **Intake dedupe:** resubmitting the same claim (same business identifier) must not create a second `ClaimResponse` — needs an idempotency key / claim identifier.
- **FHIR writes:** on retry, use conditional create (`If-None-Exist`) so a network retry doesn't double-write artifacts.
- **Emulator call:** the legacy `ADJRXCLM` call must be retry-safe.
- **Async (if we adopt C3's Pub/Sub path):** at-least-once delivery *forces* idempotent consumers.
On referential invariants, agree: define **one decision id per adjudication** and mandatory links — `ClaimResponse.request→Claim`, `Task.focus→ClaimResponse`, `Provenance.target→[Claim,ClaimResponse]`, `RiskAssessment.basis→…`. Without these the audit chain is unprovable. Strong agree.

**7. Archived PRD commands — agree, Low.**
Confirmed §11.3 uses `Authorization: Bearer $FHIR_API_KEY`, but our Kong uses the `apikey` header — copy-paste would fail against our platform. Agree with a warning block. Cheap, worth doing.

**8. Test strategy incomplete — agree, Critical.**
"Per-service tests" ([plan.md:176](docs/phase2/plan.md#L176)) is inadequate for a growing rules engine. Agree with your matrix, and I'd bind it to points 5 & 6: **rules golden tests** (claim → expected decision, per rule *and combinations* — the aggregation cases), **API contract tests** (schema/error taxonomy), **e2e golden paths** (the 4–5 demo scenarios), **non-regression snapshots** on `ClaimResponse`, **idempotency/replay tests**, and a **Phase-1-independence test** (`docker compose up` starts only Phase 1). Golden-fixture governance (where they live, how they're regenerated, review policy) should be explicit.

**Final note (archival banner) — agree.** Same fix as #7: strengthen the `source-prd.md` banner to "archival, non-normative, superseded by requirements.md — do not execute commands as-is."

## Two things you didn't flag that I'd add
- **Agent/determinism boundary isn't asserted in the contract.** The claims-agent explains; it must be stated as **non-authoritative** and *outside* the decision contract, so the LLM can never alter a deterministic outcome. This protects point 5.
- **Triage's single-result return under-reports for aggregation.** `POST /triage/refill-risk` returns the *first* matching `RuleResult` only. If a patient has both a penicillin conflict *and* a duplicate therapy, adjudication sees one. Fine for a HIGH gate; limiting for a complete "reasons" list. This is a genuine consequence of the D1 reuse decision and belongs in the contract discussion.

## What I'd change (for your approval — not doing it yet)
1. Reconcile **R10 ↔ C2**; make DB-less Kong the canonical Phase 2 gateway; add a **gateway-strangler migration/rollback/ownership** subsection.
2. Make **Cloud Run isolation controls normative**; demote GKE/NetworkPolicy to a labeled fallback; fix the intra-plan conflict.
3. Replace the **committed dev key** with generated-at-startup, acceptance criterion = still zero-setup.
4. Add a **per-milestone cloud-touchpoint** distinction; rebrand M8 as "Phase 2b — Cloud" with its own DoD (keep the design).
5. Add a normative **"Decision Contract"** section: outcome precedence + aggregation, triage→outcome mapping, canonical schemas, error taxonomy, agent-non-authoritative clause.
6. Add **referential-invariant + idempotency** requirements (one decision id, mandatory links, the four idempotency sites).
7. Strengthen **source-prd** banner + add a "commands illustrative, not runnable as-is" note.
8. Add a **minimum test matrix** + golden-fixture governance.

Two questions before I touch anything:
- On **#2**, do you agree we keep Cloud Run canonical (my recommendation) rather than maintaining dual GKE/Cloud Run control models — or do you actually want both documented as first-class?
- On **#4**, are you okay keeping the cloud *design* in-plan (just better fenced), or do you want the deep cloud detail physically relocated to a separate doc?

On #2. I am worrid abot a lot of rework of a working Phase 1 system if we eliminate GKE. Comment on that please.

On #4, there was a misunderstanding. I want even more focus on cloud, and if possible stubs or tests included in earlier phases. Actually, expand and intensify the cloud focus, just be very clear what deliverables stakeholders will get, depending on the type of stakeholder, after each milestone. Ask for more clarification if I am vacillating here!

Both are good refinements. Let me address #2 first (reassurance + a reframe), then #4 (you've flipped the ask — I want to make sure I intensify in the direction you actually mean).

## On #2 — you will NOT rework Phase 1. My "fallback" wording caused this; let me fix the framing.

The worry is well-placed *given how I phrased it*, but the actual design has **zero Phase 1 rework**. "Cloud Run canonical" was never meant as "rip out GKE." Here's the real shape:

- **Phase 1 stays exactly as it is on GKE** — `deploy.sh`, the KIC/Helm Kong, and the HAPI `fhir-service` Deployment are untouched. That's the whole isolation principle, and it's what `phase1-v1` protects.
- **Cloud Run is purely additive for the *new* Phase 2 services** (`claims-service`, `rxclaim-emulator`, `claims-agent`). Nothing existing moves.
- Key fact that dissolves most of the worry: **`triage` and `mcp-agent` are not in the cloud today at all.** `deploy.sh` only deploys Kong + `fhir-service`; triage/agent are local-compose-only. So putting `triage` on Cloud Run for Phase 2 is **greenfield, not a migration.**
- **HAPI stays on GKE** (always-on, per C1's cold-start reasoning) — no change.

So the correct model isn't "Cloud Run vs GKE" (which implied migrating Phase 1). It's a deliberate **hybrid, split by phase/component**:

| Plane | Runs on | Rework? |
|---|---|---|
| Phase 1: KIC Kong + HAPI | **GKE (as today)** | none |
| Phase 2: claims-service, rxclaim-emulator, claims-agent, triage-in-cloud | **Cloud Run (new)** | greenfield |

And this **also resolves your point-2 inconsistency cleanly, without a dual control model:** each component uses its *own platform's* native control — GKE workloads (Phase 1) keep GKE controls; Cloud Run workloads (Phase 2) use `ingress=internal` + IAM. NetworkPolicy simply doesn't apply to the emulator because the emulator runs on Cloud Run, not GKE. There's no component with two competing control models — the docs just need to say "controls follow the platform each component runs on," and stop asserting NetworkPolicy for a Cloud Run service.

The **one genuine cross-phase artifact is the gateway**: during transition you'd have KIC Kong (Phase 1, `/fhir`) *and* DB-less Kong (Phase 2). That's the gateway-strangler I described in point 1 — Phase 1's Kong keeps working untouched; a later, reversible step folds `/fhir` onto the DB-less Kong only when you choose. So even the gateway involves no *forced* Phase 1 rework.

Net: I'd rewrite the docs to say **"hybrid: GKE for Phase 1 (untouched) + Cloud Run for Phase 2 (new)"** instead of "canonical/fallback." Does that fully address the rework concern? If so, I'll drop the "GKE fallback" framing entirely.

## On #4 — understood, you want MORE cloud, pulled earlier. This reverses D8, so let me pin the intensity precisely.

Two things to flag before I expand:

1. **This changes decision D8** ("Phase 2 is local-first; cloud deferred"). Intensifying cloud and pulling stubs/tests earlier means cloud becomes a **first-class thread through every milestone**, not a back-loaded M8. That's fine and compatible with Phase 1 independence (still additive) — but D8 needs to be rewritten, and I want to be explicit that we're doing that.

2. **"Intensify cloud" spans a wide cost/complexity range**, and you invited me to push on where you might be vacillating — this is exactly that spot. There's a big difference between *designing/stubbing/testing* cloud continuously versus *actually deploying live* to GCP from early milestones (real spend, secrets, CI-to-cloud, teardown discipline). I don't want to guess.

Here's the concrete shape I'd propose regardless of intensity — cloud woven through each milestone:
- Every service ships its **Terraform + Cloud Run config** from *its own* milestone (not M8).
- **Cloud contract + smoke tests** per service run in CI from M2 onward.
- The **C3 repository seam** is tested against Postgres *and* a NoSQL emulator early, proving the scale-swap.
- **OpenTelemetry tracing + health/readiness** wired from M3, not retrofitted.
- A **stakeholder × milestone deliverables matrix** so each audience knows what they get when. Illustrative sliver:

| After… | Exec/Business | Solution Architect | Developer | Security/Compliance | SRE/Platform |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **M2** | "legacy core is wrapped" narrative | ACL boundary + emulator contract | emulator API + golden fixtures | injection-safe queries reviewed | Terraform module + Cloud Run stub deploys in CI |
| **M4** | first adjudicated claim demo | decision contract + trace of one claim | ClaimResponse schema + rules golden tests | PHI-safe logging verified | OTel traces in Cloud Trace; smoke test green |
| **M7** | full local demo, all golden paths | end-to-end architecture proof | full test matrix passing | audit-chain + idempotency evidence | preview-env deploy runbook |

To fill that in properly, I need two calls from you:

Both answers are clear and they fully resolve #2 and #4:

- **#2 → hybrid, no Phase 1 rework.** I'll drop the "canonical/fallback" framing entirely and document it as **GKE for Phase 1 (untouched) + Cloud Run for Phase 2 (new)**, with controls following each component's platform. Your rework worry is unfounded once phrased this way, and it also fixes the point-2 inconsistency.
- **#4 → "design + stub + test throughout, deploy late."** Cloud becomes a first-class thread through every milestone (Terraform/Cloud Run config, contract + smoke tests against emulators/stubs, OTel from M3, the C3 repository seam tested against Postgres *and* a NoSQL emulator) — but **no live GCP spend until a late milestone**. This **rewrites D8** from "cloud deferred" to "cloud designed/stubbed/tested continuously; live deploy is Phase 2b." Stakeholder matrix covers all six audiences (Exec/Business, Product, Architect, Developer, Security/Compliance, SRE/Platform).

Here's the **consolidated change manifest** I'd apply to the docs PR (#24). Nothing changed yet — this is for your go/no-go, and you can veto any line.

**`requirements.md`**
1. **R10** — reconcile with C2: DB-less Kong is the canonical Phase 2 gateway; Phase 1 KIC Kong untouched; hybrid stated explicitly. *(fixes #1)*
2. **R11** — emulator isolation = Cloud Run `ingress=internal` + IAM; "controls follow the platform"; stop asserting NetworkPolicy as *the* control. *(fixes #2)*
3. **Dev key** (R10/§gateway) — replace committed key with **generated-at-startup**, acceptance criterion = still zero manual steps (gitleaks-clean). *(fixes #3)*
4. **New R17 — Decision Contract:** outcome precedence + multi-reason aggregation (adjudication is accumulate-then-resolve, *not* triage's first-match), triage→outcome mapping, canonical Claim/ClaimResponse schemas + error taxonomy, **agent-output-non-authoritative** clause. *(fixes #5)*
5. **New R18 — Audit invariants + idempotency:** one decision id per adjudication, mandatory resource links, and idempotency at the four sites (intake dedupe, FHIR conditional create, emulator retry, async at-least-once). *(fixes #6)*
6. **New R19 — Test matrix + golden-fixture governance.** *(fixes #8)*
7. **Rewrite D8** → cloud designed/stubbed/tested throughout; live deploy = Phase 2b. Adjust out-of-scope (NoSQL/BigQuery still deferred; live cloud deploy is *late*, not out-of-scope). *(implements #4)*

**`plan.md`**
8. Reframe §1/§2/§5 to **hybrid GKE+Cloud Run**; fix the intra-plan NetworkPolicy-vs-internal-ingress conflict (L66 vs L124). *(#2)*
9. Add a **gateway-strangler** subsection: state transition, rollback, ownership. *(#1)*
10. **Intensify cloud across M2–M7** (artifacts/stubs/tests per milestone) + add per-milestone cloud touchpoints; rebrand M8 → **"Phase 2b — Cloud (live deploy)."** *(#4)*
11. Add **Decision Contract**, **Audit/idempotency**, **Test matrix**, and **Stakeholder × milestone deliverables matrix** (6 audiences) sections. *(#4,#5,#6,#8)*
12. Update §8 risks accordingly.

**`README.md`** — update C2 to hybrid; surface the cloud-throughout posture + stakeholder matrix.
**`source-prd.md`** — strengthen the archival banner and add a "commands illustrative, not runnable as-is" note near the §11 command blocks. *(#7 + your final note)*

- The new **R17/R18 decision-contract + idempotency** content is normative design. Do you want me to **specify it concretely** (precedence matrix, tie-breaks, example payloads, the four idempotency mechanisms) — my recommendation — or keep it as *requirements-to-be-detailed* placeholders so you can shape the semantics yourself first?

42	### R4 — Benefit + prior-authorization rules (new, deterministic, Java)
43	A deterministic rules engine covering the **new** adjudication domains:
44	- **Eligibility** — coverage active on the date of service.
45	- **Formulary** — on/off formulary, tier, PA flag, quantity limit.
46	- **Prior authorization** — high-cost / flagged drugs require PA on file.
47	- **Benefit / quantity / age** rules as needed to reach the rule-count target below.
48	
49	Rules are **layered** (per PRD §9.5) so the layers can change independently:
50	1. Federal/public policy (CMS NCD/LCD-inspired).
51	2. Plan configuration (per plan design).
52	3. Customer-specific overrides.
53	
54	**Rule-count target (canonical):** a representative **15–20 rules across ~8
55	domains** (eligibility, provider, formulary, prior-auth, clinical, coding, medical
56	necessity, quantity). Not all need to be exercised by the demo.
57	
58	### R5 — Clinical safety (REUSED, not rebuilt)
59	Drug-allergy and duplicate-therapy checks are **not reimplemented**. The claims
60	façade calls the **existing Phase 1 `triage-service`** (`POST /triage/refill-risk`,
61	unchanged) over HTTP for clinical-safety evaluation. This is the CDS sub-module.
62	
63	### R6 — Decision artefacts (FHIR, Da Vinci-aware, generic)
64	Each adjudication persists auditable FHIR R4 resources to the existing HAPI server:
65	- `Claim` / `ClaimResponse` (approve / reject / pend / route-to-review).
66	- `Task` for manual review when routed.
67	- `Provenance` (one per decision) and `RiskAssessment` for the audit trail.
68	- `CoverageEligibilityResponse` where appropriate.
69	
70	Resources are **structured and named to nod to Da Vinci PAS / CRD and CMS-0057-F**
71	but are **generic R4** — full PAS profile conformance is out of scope (see D6).
72	
73	### R7 — Explanation agent (SEPARATE from Phase 1 agent)
74	A dedicated **`claims-agent`** calls the claims façade and explains, in natural
75	language, why a claim was approved, rejected, pended, or routed — in the style of
76	PRD §9.4. It is a **new, separate agent**, not an extension of the Phase 1
77	`mcp-agent`. It holds **no clinical/business logic** (that lives in the services).
78	It may share only non-clinical plumbing (Anthropic client setup, tool-loop
79	scaffolding, output formatting) with the Phase 1 agent.

81	### R8 — Runnable demo
82	The whole flow runs locally via Docker Compose, seeded with a dedicated claims
83	demo dataset, producing 4–5 golden-path outcomes:
84	1. **Approved** — on-formulary, tier 1, coverage active, no conflicts.
85	2. **Rejected** — coverage inactive on date of service.
86	3. **Pended → review Task** — high-cost drug, no PA on file.
87	4. **Safety alert** — penicillin allergy + amoxicillin (reuses Phase 1 triage; ties Phase 1 → Phase 2).
88	5. *(stretch)* **Multi-reason** — non-formulary + quantity limit (matches PRD §9.4 sample).
